The side auto uses while the surface cannot be measured. Ignored unless mode is auto.

defineTheme(input) -> DefinedTheme; tokens are any `--*` name (the closed upstream union is the pipeline's token set, checked by pnpm tokens:check); icons take IconDefinition/IconLoader (registerIcons shape), indicators are an opaque registry the indicator family reads; `syntax` takes the structural SyntaxThemeDefinition.

Emits @scope ([data-tct-theme="<name>"]) to ([data-tct-theme]); component keys resolve to tag + part (theming-targets.js), prop:value keys to reflected host attributes. Golden-tested against tokens.css for the Tecton theme.
Targets [data-media-theme="dark|light"], the attribute tct-media-theme writes and tokens.css pins.
The seed of accent-less (neutral-only) configs is the Tecton accent hue (#644a78), guarded against --color-accent by a test.

React hooks and context. The published theme is themeContext (core/context/keys.js), provided by tct-theme (WP-F) and tct-media-theme; wiring tct-theme.theme to a DefinedTheme is in the hand-off.
Owned by the syntax-theme provider work package; defineTheme reads its result through the structural SyntaxThemeDefinition type.

differences.text: display: contents and no background painting, as the upstream wrapper (which documents that it does not add a background). ARCHITECTURE §8.1 lists tct-media-theme with the theme-island rule (display: block, paints a background); that rule fits tct-theme, which owns its subtree. A media theme sits on a surface its parent already paints and mode="auto" measures that surface, so painting one would feed back into its own input. The block paint is left to tct-theme.
mode defaults to auto (upstream requires it, so an element without a mode has no upstream meaning). Both mode and fallback reflect.

The attribute is data-media-theme (upstream data-astryx-media, dataAttr("media")), the selector the token pipeline emits its onDark/onLight blocks for (styling.md §7). The element also publishes the resolved side through themeContext.

auto measures the parent in the flat tree: it crosses slots (a media theme slotted into tct-card measures the card's painted base) and shadow roots, skips display: contents boxes, and parses color(srgb …) and, through a one-pixel canvas, any other colour space. It re-measures on ancestor style/class/data-theme/hidden changes, on prefers-color-scheme changes, on reconnect and on mode/fallback changes, instead of on every React render. A stylesheet swap alone is not observable: switch mode to off and back.

D-005: the focus ring and its inner ring (--tecton-color-focus-inner) are light-dark() tokens, so the media block pinning color-scheme re-points them to the side of the surface with no component rule. Tested against the [data-theme] island values. Without light-dark() (Tier 2) only the pinned roles follow.

requests.reason: Generate the theme wiring data the runtime cannot import: (1) a token-defaults module from tokens.json (name to light/dark value) so core need not depend on the tokens package (tokenDefaults is a registry until then; tct-theme should call registerTokenDefaults(tokenDefaultsFromMetadata(tokens)) with @tecton-wc/tokens/tokens.js), and (2) the theming-target table from custom-elements.json with themingTargetsFromCem(), registered at start-up, so a theme component key resolves to its element and part (until then a key falls back to tct-<key> with part "base" plus the built-in text, heading, button and icon parts).

Add packages/core/src/theme to the upstream Astryx (MIT) list of adapted code (defineTheme and the CSS generators, adaptations, scale expanders, contrast and colour parsing). hct.ts ports Google material-color-utilities (Apache-2.0, via Astryx): add its notice (copyright Google LLC, Apache-2.0) to the third-party list.

The scope contract the generated CSS assumes: tct-theme writes data-tct-theme="<theme name>" on its host (generateThemeCSS scopes to [data-tct-theme="<name>"] and stops at a nested [data-tct-theme]), injects the two blocks (prose into the reset layer, component into a layer after tecton.tokens; @scope needs Chrome 118, Safari 17.4, Firefox 146), and provides themeContext. Its `theme` property takes a DefinedTheme; registerTheme(theme) makes it resolvable by name for SSR.

runElementSuite asserts `element.shadowRoot` is not null after reconnecting, which a light-DOM provider (tct-media-theme, tct-theme, tct-size-provider, ...) cannot satisfy. Add a `lightDom?: boolean` option that skips that assertion. tct-media-theme runs an equivalent local lifecycle block meanwhile.

Light-DOM families ship `<tag>.light.css` (it feeds the generated light-dom.css), but only `*.styles.css` is compiled into a Lit CSSResult. tct-media-theme therefore repeats its two-line sheet in media-theme.light.ts, and a node test keeps them equal (a `?raw` import broke the build: the emitted media-theme.light.js has no .d.ts). Compiling `*.light.css` to a CSSResult like `*.styles.css` would remove the duplicate for every light-DOM family.

core.media-theme.notes: Guides: [mwg:component-specific-light-dark-theme] color-scheme pins the side and light-dark() tokens re-resolve per element; [mwg:dark-mode] color-scheme and accent-color; [mwg:contrast-color] considered and not used, it answers black or white while the choice is between the token pairs or none; [mwg:custom-elements] reconnect and connectedMoveCallback; [mwg:accessible-web-components] no role, transparent to the accessibility tree.
